submission.natural_language_explanation: L4/N159+ fires on the token that closes a fused two-token unit, i.e. the second member of a chunk that names a single lexical item: a hyphen or prefix/particle compound (in-house, after-school, out-of-date, over|harvesting, run|ny, Port|ales) or a fixed preposition/particle-headed expression (in place, in mind, into play, into force, cut short, top out, at bay, end of). Both members are required (replacing the earlier token erases essentially the whole activation, and that earlier token never fires alone), while the same words as free compositional constituents (a place, take place, your mind, in order, in line, in which, of the, in house, farmhouse, on site) and the token after the completed unit stay at baseline; the output side carries no coherent next-token set (Jacobian kurtosis 3.06, 0% agreement with the logit lens), so this is retrospective chunk-detection, not lookahead.

The Riverbend Public Works Committee met on the evening of March 14 in the community hall, with chair Dana Whitfield presiding and eleven residents present.

The first item concerned the condition of the Mill Road bridge, which has carried heavy truck traffic since the quarry expanded two years ago. Ms. Whitfield reported that the inspection completed in January found no structural failure, though the deck surface has begun to crack in several places. The committee agreed to ask the county for a full engineering assessment before any repairs are scheduled. Several residents asked whether the bridge would be closed during the work; the chair said no closure has been proposed and that any change would be announced two weeks before any closure began.

The second item concerned the summer repaving program. The committee reviewed a list of fourteen streets identified by the maintenance crew as the highest priorities. Staff noted that the cost of asphalt has risen sharply since the last contract was signed, and that the estimate prepared in February exceeds the amount budgeted for the year. After some discussion the committee voted to fund the first eight streets and to defer the remainder to the following fiscal year. A resident asked whether the deferred work would be reconsidered if additional funds became available; the chair said the list would be reviewed again in the autumn.

The third item concerned the proposal to add a sidewalk along the north side of Harbor Street, where children walk to the elementary school. The engineering department presented three options, each varying in cost and in the number of trees that would need to be removed. The least expensive option would remove four trees; the most expensive would remove one and add a small rain garden. Residents who spoke were divided, and several asked for more time to review the drawings. The committee agreed to display the plans in the library for thirty days and to collect written comments before returning to the question.

The fourth item concerned the repaving work planned for the industrial park. Staff explained that the contractor selected in December had failed to secure the required bonds, and that consequently the repaving contract was put on hold in March while the legal department reviewed the terms. The chair asked how long the delay might last; staff said the review could take six to eight weeks and that the work would not begin until it was complete. A member asked whether the delay would affect the schedule for the school sidewalk, and staff said the two projects are funded from different accounts and would proceed independently.

The fifth item concerned a request from the historical society for permission to place a small marker near the old mill. The committee approved the request provided the society confirms that the marker will not obstruct the path.

One resident then asked about the condition of the storm drains along Front Street, which flooded twice last spring. Staff said the drains had been cleared in the autumn but that debris from the construction site had collected again, and that a crew would return the following week.

The meeting adjourned at 8:40 p.m. The next meeting is scheduled for April 11 in the community hall.
